title: Turing's 1937 model of calculation

body: A. M. Turing's paper "On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem" appeared in the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society in 1937. It defines computable numbers by describing a machine with a finite table of instructions and a tape it can read, write, and move. A number is computable if such a machine can write out its digits. Turing uses the model to show that there is no general method that decides, for every statement of a sufficiently rich formal system, whether the statement is provable. That is the application to the decision problem named in the title. The paper is a mathematical definition and a negative theorem. It is not a description of an electronic computer, which came later and was influenced by this and related work. Calling every laptop "a Turing machine" is a loose analogy to the model, not a claim in the 1937 paper.
